subject: Q1 headroom advance notice + autoscale exception request
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Sara Klein <sara.k@helioshealth.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Q1 headroom advance notice + autoscale exception request

Hi team,

Heads up — Helios Health (Sara on cc) wants to run a 3-week production pilot in early Jan that will push steady low-latency traffic at peak times (estimated 200k inference tokens/day; see attached forecast). They asked if we can guarantee a dedicated pool slice for the pilot window or make a narrow autoscale-exception so their SLA-driven jobs don't see throttling.

Key asks from Helios:
- Dedicated slice of ~4 GPUs for 3 weeks starting 2027-01-08 (customer flexible ±3 days)
- A policy exception so autoscaler doesn’t evict during business hours (08:00–20:00 PT) for latency-sensitive endpoints
- Short runbook + rollback plan (I attached a draft runbook)

As product lead and capacity ops, I want to align on:
- Product / SLO implications if we carve this from the Q1 pilot pool
- Ops feasibility and whether we can grant an autoscale exception for that window without impacting other enterprise pilots
- Finance approvals path for a temporary dedicated carve (Marcus) — rough cost estimate would help ASAP so I can confirm with Helios.

Proposed mitigations that might reduce the footprint: prefix caching and a quantized model variant for the pilot traffic. If we can get approval for a narrow exception (business hours only) we could avoid a full reservation.

Attachments: Q1-headroom-forecast.xlsx, pilot-runbook-draft.pdf

Next steps I propose:
1) Ops: feasibility + constraints by EOD Mon (21st)
2) Product: SLO/reserve tradeoffs + fallback variant recommendation by Tue
3) Finance: preliminary approval path and estimated chargeback by Tue

Sara — can you confirm the hard window and whether Helios will accept a scaled-down variant if we can’t secure a full 4 GPU carve?

Thanks,
Avery

--
Avery Johnson
Customer Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.example.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Sara Klein <sara.k@helioshealth.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q1 headroom advance notice + autoscale exception request

Thanks for the heads up, Avery — quick read: good opportunity but need to quantify risk.

Questions/notes:
- SLO impact: if we carve a 4-GPU slice from the pilot pool, what's the expected latency delta for other tenants during their peak? Laura — can you run a sim against our Jan usage curve?
- Autoscale exception: I’m wary of a global "do not evict" flag. If Ops can implement a time-bounded policy (business hours only) and still ensure fairness outside the window, I’m +1 for trying.
- Model variant: a quantized 7B for the pilot could reduce GPU need to 2 GPUs but might regress on hallucination/quality metrics. We should run a quick eval set against the Helios prompt set; Sara — happy to share eval guidance if you can provide representative prompts.

If we can get a clear cost and a fallback hybrid (2 dedicated + burst to 4 via autoscale within a known latency envelope), I can sign off on product side.

Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Product Lead, Dedicated Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>, Sara Klein <sara.k@helioshealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q1 headroom advance notice + autoscale exception request

Quick ops feasibility note — did a preliminary capacity check this morning against current committed pools and planned Q1 spikes. Highlights: 
- We have a short window 2027-01-07 → 2027-01-28 where reassigning a 4-GPU slice from the pilot pool is technically possible with minimal impact, provided we accept stricter preemption rules outside the business-hours window.
- Implementing a time-bound autoscale exemption is feasible but requires a temporary override flag per allocation (we've done this for two enterprise pilots before). It takes ~6–8 hours of ops effort to create, test, and document the override and ~4 hours to tear down post-window.
- Alternative: provision 2 dedicated GPUs plus a burst policy to add up to +2 on demand with a guaranteed <80ms p50 delta. That reduces cost and operational risk.

I can run the Jan sim by EOD Mon and attach projected latency curves; need the exact Helios traffic shape (hourly) to tighten the sim.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Capacity Operations Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Sara Klein <sara.k@helioshealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q1 headroom advance notice + autoscale exception request

Finance view — noted. Two quick items:
1) Chargeback: temporary carve (4 GPUs for 3 weeks) estimated at $27k list cost before discounts. If we do 2+burst the baseline is ~$15k plus variable burst charges. I can formalize these numbers into a price sheet for Helios; need to know whether they expect a single invoice or a committed reservation (month pro-rated).
2) Approval: anything above $20k one-off will need director approval plus an Ops risk sign-off. If we present 2 options (dedicated vs 2+burst) with clear cost deltas, I can expedite review.

I'll draft a short pricing summary by EOD. Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Sr. Finance Manager, Commercial | Redwood Inference

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Sara Klein <sara.k@helioshealth.com>, DevOps Ops <ops@nebulon.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Q1 headroom advance notice + autoscale exception request

Thanks all — helpful. Sara answered my question earlier this afternoon: Helios is firm on the business window (target start 2027-01-10) but will accept 2 GPUs + burst if we can guarantee p95 latency < 350ms during business hours. They prefer a single invoice with line-item for the carveout.

Next concrete asks from me: 
- Laura: please attach the Jan sim and the "2+burst" projected latency curves (EOD Tue)
- Marcus: please produce the two-line price sheet (4-GPU carve vs 2+burst) + note on approval path (EOD Tue)
- Kimberly: if you can run a 1-day eval of the quantized 7B variant against Helios prompts, that would speed up the fallback path. I can share prompts by EOD tonight (Sara will send them).

I'll prepare the customer comms and proposed canary rollback and plan to send to Helios once we have the numbers.

Avery

--
Avery Johnson
Customer Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
